question: Let $\overline{a}, \overline{b}, \overline{c}$ be three non-coplanar vectors. Then the point of intersection of the line joining the points $\overline{a}+\overline{b}+\overline{c}, \overline{a}-\overline{b}+3\overline{c}$ and the line joining the points $2\overline{a}-\overline{b}+\overline{c}$ , $\overline{a}-2\overline{b}+4\overline{c}$ is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution Take the basis $\{\overline{a},\overline{b},\overline{c}\}$ and write each point as an ordered triple of its coefficients. Let $L_1$ join $P_1=\overline{a}+\overline{b}+\overline{c}=(1,1,1)$ and $Q_1=\overline{a}-\overline{b}+3\overline{c}=(1,-1,3)$ . Then $L_1: (1,1,1)+t(0,-2,2)=(1,1-2t,1+2t)$ . Let $L_2$ join $P_2=2\overline{a}-\overline{b}+\overline{c}=(2,-1,1)$ and $Q_2=\overline{a}-2\overline{b}+4\overline{c}=(1,-2,4)$ . Then $L_2: (2,-1,1)+s(-1,-1,3)=(2-s,-1-s,1+3s)$ . At the intersection, equate coordinates: $1=2-s$ , $1-2t=-1-s$ , and $1+2t=1+3s$ . From the first equation, $s=1$ . Substitute in the second: $1-2t=-2$ , so $t=\frac{3}{2}$ . Check in the third: $1+2\cdot\frac{3}{2}=4$ and $1+3\cdot1=4$ , so the lines do intersect. The intersection is $(1,1-2t,1+2t)$ with $t=\frac{3}{2}$ , that is $(1,-2,4)$ . Converting back to vector form gives $\overline{a}-2\overline{b}+4\overline{c}$ . Hence the correct option is the one with option C. © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: The alkaline earth metals are $\mathrm{Be}$ , $\mathrm{Mg}$ , $\mathrm{Ca}$ , $\mathrm{Sr}$ , $\mathrm{Ba}$ and $\mathrm{Ra}$ . Densities of the first four members are: $\mathrm{Be} = 1.85\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ , $\mathrm{Mg} = 1.74\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ , $\mathrm{Ca} = 1.55\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ , $\mathrm{Sr} = 2.64\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ . Comparing these values, $\mathrm{Ca}$ has the smallest density, which is lower than even that of $\mathrm{Be}$ and $\mathrm{Mg}$ . This is due to the comparatively large atomic size and relatively weak metallic bonding of $\mathrm{Ca}$ in its crystal lattice, which gives it an unusually open structure. Hence the alkaline earth metal with the lowest density is $\mathrm{Ca}$ . © examsnet.com

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following amine cannot be prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis method?

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Correct answer: Phenylamine (option C) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis prepares only primary amines that can be formed through an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction on an alkyl/benzylic halide. Step 1: Phthalimide is treated with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ to form potassium phthalimide: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{CO})_2\text{NH} + \text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{CO})_2\text{N}^-\text{K}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O}$ Step 2: The phthalimide anion attacks an alkyl halide $R-X$ by an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ pathway to give $N$ -alkylphthalimide. Step 3: Alkaline hydrolysis (or hydrazinolysis) of the $N$ -alkylphthalimide liberates the primary amine $R\text{NH}_2$ . Ethylamine ( $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ ) comes from ethyl halide, propylamine ( $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{NH}_2$ ) from propyl halide, and benzylamine ( $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ ) from benzyl halide. All three of these halides are $\text{sp}^3$ (or benzylic) halides that readily undergo $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution, so their amines can be prepared this way. Phenylamine (aniline) would require chlorobenzene to react with the phthalimide anion. In chlorobenzene the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance, and the planar aryl carbon is shielded from backside attack, so nucleophilic substitution by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ does not occur. Therefore the phthalimide anion cannot be attached to a benzene ring, and phenylamine cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis. Phenylamine is instead prepared by reduction of nitrobenzene, e.g. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Sn/HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ . Hence the amine that cannot be prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is phenylamine, option C. © examsnet.com
